law.breakBefore: From Dec 10, 2026: when working hours are 4, the break may be skipped if the worker explicitly asks not to take it (new proviso to Labor Standards Act Art. 54(1)).
law.breakAfter: When working hours are 4, the break may be skipped if the worker explicitly asks not to take it (LSA Art. 54(1) proviso, effective Dec 10, 2026). It requires the worker's request; the employer cannot drop it unilaterally. If you worked without a break, turn off auto-apply and enter 0 minutes.
law.breakWaiverWarn: However, on days with 4 working hours the break may be skipped if the worker explicitly requested it (Art. 54(1) proviso).
law.eiBefore: * Employment insurance: until Dec 31, 2026 you are covered if you work 60+ hours a month (15+ h/week) or for 3+ consecutive months. From Jan 1, 2027 coverage depends on pay (income) instead of hours; the threshold will be set by Enforcement Decree (reflected once final) (Employment Insurance Act Art. 10, Act No. 21473).
law.eiAfter: * Employment insurance: from Jan 1, 2027 you are covered if your pay at that workplace meets the income threshold, regardless of hours. The threshold is set by Enforcement Decree (reflected once final). Daily workers and those employed 3+ consecutive months are covered even below it, and people with two or more jobs can apply to combine pay (Employment Insurance Act Art. 10).
